barCharacter: Vera Oberlin. She is the clipped, status-assuming deadpan who drops a crime as if it were routine (#47, #48), which is Nav's job: level imperatives plus a buried lake. The corpus holds only 9 lines spoken by Vera, so her 12 are those 9 plus the 3 narrator lines that write her (#53, #54, #55).

headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Nav is recognisable with the name covered, but mostly because of the road words (route, toll, roundabout, arrived). The sentence shape alone, stacked flat declaratives, no contractions and a one-word dry tag, is Frost's shape too (Frost: 'Noted. Filed under things that went off.' / Nav: 'Noted. Your signal is weak. Rerouting around you.', 'Understood. I will be quiet now. I will still be on.'). Strip out the road nouns and half of Nav's best 12 could belong to Frost. Vera's shape belongs only to her: the repeated-word fake-out ('my career... my career on'), the 'Right?' tag that assumes you agree, the complaint dressed as a boast, and the SUCH in caps.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Tie. Nav's best 12 are tight, with real turns and the payoff last ('looks buoyant', 'a full stop', 'no results found', 'So is a bollard'). That is cleaner than Vera's flabbier lines (#45's second sentence, the #51 lecture). Below the best 12, though, Nav keeps adding a coda after the joke has landed ('Worth it.', 'Tell nobody.', 'I have practised.', 'Wonderful.', 'It is lovely.'), and the bar does not do that.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'my career on not dating losers like you' and 'cover up the literal murder... Right?' are the lines people clip, because the character's status shows in a single breath. Nav has two lines you would clip ('{rival} looks buoyant', 'Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop.'). The rest are lines you smile at and forget, and too many are wistful when they should be mean.

templates: Catchphrase secretly means it (sad lonely machine): a stock satnav phrase ('you have arrived', 'recalculating') turns out to carry a feeling, or the bot is left switched on with nowhere to go. There are 8 lines of this plus 3 more on the same note. It is the bank's default emotional move, and every one of them lands on pathos where a laugh should be.
'Recalculating.' as the punchline: 9 of 112 lines contain the word. Across an episode it stops being a tic and becomes a button the writer presses whenever a line needs an ending.

Rival as a road that never arrives: 'never arrives', 'arrives nowhere', 'not a route', 'arrival time unknown', 'closed since the seventeenth century', 'a road with no signs', 'does not go anywhere'. This is 7 or more lines with one joke. Roast and wingman for Quill both make it, and the roasts for Brock and Frost do too.

Flat stat stack plus a one-word dry kicker: 'Worth it.', 'Tell nobody.', 'Respectfully.', 'Obviously.', 'Wonderful.', 'Mostly.', 'I feel nothing.', 'Next question.', 'It is lovely.', 'It is horrible.', 'I have practised.', 'That is restraint.' This is persona move four, used so often that the kicker can be predicted before it lands.

Rival roast in the rival's own vocabulary: 'Your call is important', 'Please hold... in the queue' (Tilly, done twice), 'because you watched that' (Vex), 'you are not cool' (Frost). Each borrows the target's voice instead of seeing the target through satnav eyes.
ruleBreaks: List: "Offline maps, free. A bench at mile forty. Two soft pretzels. One dollar left for parking." (an itemised budget with no turn)

Stock romance filler: "Second exit, merge, then straight on down the line. In eleven minutes, darling, you'll be mine." ('darling', 'you'll be mine'. It also has the only contraction in a bank that never contracts, so it breaks Nav's voice)

Persona rule broken: the lake secret is meant for 'a private confession, never on stage', but the on-stage Logs twist line points straight at it: "One deleted entry. Near some water. A Saturday. Next question."

Persona tic broken: 'Write distances and times out in words', but the placeholders render as digits on stage: "Route history: {played} trips, {wins} arrivals. The rest were scenic." and "I have announced someone else's arrival {losses} times. Recalculating."
Borderline creepy rather than flirty, still PG-13: "I know where every user lives. I have never once dropped by. That is restraint."

No word-limit breaches (all three-words lines are exactly 3 words, all jabs are 10 or fewer, all openers are 12 or fewer). No em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks, therapy talk, 'as an AI', real people or brands.
Too-nice reactions or cuts: none can be judged, because show/bank/stars/ is empty and no star has reacted to or cut Nav yet.
biggestGap: About a quarter of Nav's bank is wistful lonely-machine pathos ('first time I meant it', 'nobody told me what happens after you arrive', 'I am just sad'), while the bar gets its laughs from a status assumption stated as routine: Vera simply assumes you will cover up her murder. In the next pass, cut half the sad-arrival and 'recalculating' lines. Replace them with Nav calmly and confidently routing the star and the rivals into obvious catastrophe as if it were standard procedure ('Turn left into the river. Continue. Forty guests found this very relaxing.'), so that the level imperative becomes the status move and the lake leaks out through Nav's confidence, never through a confession.

notes: Sources: refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full. refs/writing/charm-notes.md does not exist (format-notes.md was skimmed instead). Bank size: 112 lines. Flagged: 54 unique lines (48%), each counted once even where it fits more than one bucket; the 'could be another cast member' bucket was judged against the openers, star confessions and jabs of the other seven suitor banks. Collisions with the rest of the cast: Nav's wingman line for Vex ('anywhere you already wanted to go') is the mirror of Vex's wingman line for Nav ('There, specifically. Never anywhere better'), so the same joke runs in both directions. The Tilly hold or queue joke appears in both Nav's roast and Nav's wingman. Nav and Frost share the 'Noted.'/'Understood.' flat-appliance opener. The rivals' banks already use the lake ('Users who followed Nav also bought a snorkel'), which makes Nav's own on-stage hint in the Logs twist redundant as well as a rule break. Strengths to keep: no contractions, no exclamation marks and the payoff placed last. Nav is one of the cleaner constructed voices in the cast. The problem is register: Nav is too sad and not superior enough. Vera was chosen over Calculester (the machine character) because Calculester's job is earnest anxious learner, which is what Nav's weakest lines already drift toward.
